title: अंश ३ · अध्याय ११

items.text: (गृहस्थसदाचाराणां मूत्रपुरीषोत्सर्गविधेश्च वर्णनम्)
items.tr: (gṛhasthasadācārāṇāṃ mūtrapurīṣotsargavidheśca varṇanam)

items.speaker: सगर उवाच
items.text:
गृहस्थस्य सदाचारं श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं मुने ।
लोकादस्मात् परस्माच्च यमातिष्ठन्न हीयते ॥१॥
items.tr:
gṛhasthasya sadācāraṃ śrotumicchāmyahaṃ mune |
lokādasmāt parasmācca yamātiṣṭhanna hīyate ||1||

items.speaker: और्व उवाच
items.text:
श्रूयतां पृथिवीपाल सदाचारस्य लक्षणम् ।
सदाचारवता पुंसा जितौ लोकावुभावपि ॥२॥
items.tr:
śrūyatāṃ pṛthivīpāla sadācārasya lakṣaṇam |
sadācāravatā puṃsā jitau lokāvubhāvapi ||2||

items.text:
साधवः क्षीणदोषास्तु सच्छब्दः साधुवाचकः ।
तेषामाचरणं यस्तु सदाचारस्स उच्यते ॥३॥
items.tr:
sādhavaḥ kṣīṇadoṣāstu sacchabdaḥ sādhuvācakaḥ |
teṣāmācaraṇaṃ yastu sadācārassa ucyate ||3||

items.text:
सप्तर्षयोऽथ मनवः प्रजानां पतयस्तथा ।
सदाचारस्य वक्तारः कर्तारश्च महीपते ॥४॥
items.tr:
saptarṣayo'tha manavaḥ prajānāṃ patayastathā |
sadācārasya vaktāraḥ kartāraśca mahīpate ||4||

items.text:
ब्राह्मे मुहूर्त्ते चोत्थाय मनसा मतिमान्नृप ।
प्रबुद्धश्चिन्तयेद्धर्ममर्थं चाप्यविरोधिनम् ॥५॥
items.tr:
brāhme muhūrtte cotthāya manasā matimānnṛpa |
prabuddhaścintayeddharmamarthaṃ cāpyavirodhinam ||5||

items.text:
अपीडया तयोः काममुभयोरपि चिन्तयेत् ।
दृष्टादृष्टविनाशाय त्रिवर्गे समदर्शिता ॥६॥
items.tr:
apīḍayā tayoḥ kāmamubhayorapi cintayet |
dṛṣṭādṛṣṭavināśāya trivarge samadarśitā ||6||

items.text:
परित्यजेदर्थकामौ धर्मपीडाकरौ नृप ।
धर्ममप्यसुखोदर्कं लोकविद्वेष्टमेव च ॥७॥
items.tr:
parityajedarthakāmau dharmapīḍākarau nṛpa |
dharmamapyasukhodarkaṃ lokavidveṣṭameva ca ||7||

items.text: ततः कल्यं समुत्थाय कुर्यान्मैत्रं नरेश्वर ॥८॥
items.tr: tataḥ kalyaṃ samutthāya kuryānmaitraṃ nareśvara ||8||

items.text:
नैरृत्यामिषुविक्षेपमतीत्याभ्यधिकं भुवः ।
दूरादावसथान्मूत्रं पुरीषं च विसर्जयेत् ॥९॥
items.tr:
nairṛtyāmiṣuvikṣepamatītyābhyadhikaṃ bhuvaḥ |
dūrādāvasathānmūtraṃ purīṣaṃ ca visarjayet ||9||

items.text: पादावनेजनोच्छिष्टे प्रक्षिपेन्न गृहाङ्गणे ॥१०॥
items.tr: pādāvanejanocchiṣṭe prakṣipenna gṛhāṅgaṇe ||10||

items.text:
आत्मच्छायां तरुच्छायां गोसूर्याग्न्यनिलांस्तथा ।
गुरुद्विजादींस्तु बुधो नाधिमेहेत् कदाचन ॥११॥
items.tr:
ātmacchāyāṃ tarucchāyāṃ gosūryāgnyanilāṃstathā |
gurudvijādīṃstu budho nādhimehet kadācana ||11||

items.text:
न कृष्टे सस्यमध्ये वा गोव्रजे जनसंसदि ।
न वर्त्मनि न नद्यादितीर्थेषु पुरुषर्षभ ॥१२॥
items.tr:
na kṛṣṭe sasyamadhye vā govraje janasaṃsadi |
na vartmani na nadyāditīrtheṣu puruṣarṣabha ||12||

items.text:
नाप्सु नैवाम्भसस्तीरे श्मशाने न समाचरेत् ।
उत्सर्गं वै पुरीषस्य मूत्रस्य च विसर्जनम् ॥१३॥
items.tr:
nāpsu naivāmbhasastīre śmaśāne na samācaret |
utsargaṃ vai purīṣasya mūtrasya ca visarjanam ||13||

items.text:
उदङ्मुखो दिवा मूत्रं विपरीतमुखो निशि ।
कुर्वीतानापदि प्राज्ञो मूत्रोत्सर्गं च पार्थिव ॥१४॥
items.tr:
udaṅmukho divā mūtraṃ viparītamukho niśi |
kurvītānāpadi prājño mūtrotsargaṃ ca pārthiva ||14||

items.text:
तृणैरास्तीर्य वसुधां वस्त्रप्रावृतमस्तकः ।
तिष्ठेन्नातिचिरं तत्र नैव किंचिदुदीरयेत् ॥१५॥
items.tr:
tṛṇairāstīrya vasudhāṃ vastraprāvṛtamastakaḥ |
tiṣṭhennāticiraṃ tatra naiva kiṃcidudīrayet ||15||

items.text:
वल्मीकमूषिकोद्भूतां मृदं नान्तर्जलां तथा ।
शौचावशिष्टां गेहाच्च नादद्याल्लेपसम्भवाम् ॥१६॥
items.tr:
valmīkamūṣikodbhūtāṃ mṛdaṃ nāntarjalāṃ tathā |
śaucāvaśiṣṭāṃ gehācca nādadyāllepasambhavām ||16||

items.text:
अणुप्राण्युपपन्नां च हलोत्खातां च पार्थिव ।
परित्यजेन्मृदो ह्येतास्सकलाश्शौचकर्मणि ॥१७॥
items.tr:
aṇuprāṇyupapannāṃ ca halotkhātāṃ ca pārthiva |
parityajenmṛdo hyetāssakalāśśaucakarmaṇi ||17||

items.text:
एका लिंगे गुदे तिस्रो दश वामकरे नृप ।
हस्तद्वये च सप्त स्युर्मृदश्शौचोपपादिकाः ॥१८॥
items.tr:
ekā liṃge gude tisro daśa vāmakare nṛpa |
hastadvaye ca sapta syurmṛdaśśaucopapādikāḥ ||18||

items.text:
अच्छेनागन्धलेपेन जलेनाबुद्बुदेन च ।
आचामेच्च मृदं भूयस्तथा दद्यात् समाहितः ॥१९॥
items.tr:
acchenāgandhalepena jalenābudbudena ca |
ācāmecca mṛdaṃ bhūyastathā dadyāt samāhitaḥ ||19||

items.text:
निष्पादिताङ्घ्रिशौचस्तु पादावभ्युक्ष्य वै पुनः ।
त्रिः पिबेत्सलिलं तेन तथा द्विः परिमार्जयेत् ॥२०॥
items.tr:
niṣpāditāṅghriśaucastu pādāvabhyukṣya vai punaḥ |
triḥ pibetsalilaṃ tena tathā dviḥ parimārjayet ||20||

items.text:
शीर्षण्यानि ततः खानि मूर्द्धानं च समालभेत् ।
बाहू नाभिं च तोयेन हृदयं चापि संस्पृशेत् ॥२१॥
items.tr:
śīrṣaṇyāni tataḥ khāni mūrddhānaṃ ca samālabhet |
bāhū nābhiṃ ca toyena hṛdayaṃ cāpi saṃspṛśet ||21||

items.text:
आचांतस्तु ततः कुर्यात् पुमान् केशप्रसाधनम् ।
आदर्शाञ्जनमाङ्गल्यं दूर्वाद्यालम्भनानि च ॥२२॥
items.tr:
ācāṃtastu tataḥ kuryāt pumān keśaprasādhanam |
ādarśāñjanamāṅgalyaṃ dūrvādyālambhanāni ca ||22||

items.text:
ततस्स्ववर्णधर्मेण वृत्त्यर्थं च धनार्जनम् ।
कुर्वीत श्रद्धासंपन्नो यजेच्च पृथिवीपते ॥२३॥
items.tr:
tatassvavarṇadharmeṇa vṛttyarthaṃ ca dhanārjanam |
kurvīta śraddhāsaṃpanno yajecca pṛthivīpate ||23||

items.text:
सोमसंस्था हविस्संस्थाः पाकसंस्थास्तु संस्थिताः ।
धने यतो मनुष्याणां यतेतातो धनार्जने ॥२४॥
items.tr:
somasaṃsthā havissaṃsthāḥ pākasaṃsthāstu saṃsthitāḥ |
dhane yato manuṣyāṇāṃ yatetāto dhanārjane ||24||

items.text:
नदीनदतटाकेषु देवखातजलेषु च ।
नित्यक्रियार्थं स्नायीत गिरिप्रस्रवणेषु च ॥२५॥
items.tr:
nadīnadataṭākeṣu devakhātajaleṣu ca |
nityakriyārthaṃ snāyīta giriprasravaṇeṣu ca ||25||

items.text:
कूपेषूद्धृततोयेन स्नानं कुर्वीत वा भुवि ।
गृहेषूद्धृततोयेन ह्यथवा भुव्यसम्भवे ॥२६॥
items.tr:
kūpeṣūddhṛtatoyena snānaṃ kurvīta vā bhuvi |
gṛheṣūddhṛtatoyena hyathavā bhuvyasambhave ||26||

items.text:
शुचिवस्त्रधरः स्नातो देवर्षिपितृतर्पणम् ।
तेषामेव हि तीर्थेन कुर्वीत सुसमाहितः ॥२७॥
items.tr:
śucivastradharaḥ snāto devarṣipitṛtarpaṇam |
teṣāmeva hi tīrthena kurvīta susamāhitaḥ ||27||

items.text:
त्रिरपः प्रीणनार्थाय देवानामपवर्जयेत् ।
ऋषीणां च यथान्यायं सकृच्चापि प्रजापतेः ॥२८॥
items.tr:
trirapaḥ prīṇanārthāya devānāmapavarjayet |
ṛṣīṇāṃ ca yathānyāyaṃ sakṛccāpi prajāpateḥ ||28||

items.text:
पितॄणां प्रीणनार्थाय तदपः पृथिवीपते ।
पितामहेभ्यश्च तथा प्रीणयेत्प्रपितामहान् ॥२९॥
items.tr:
pitṝṇāṃ prīṇanārthāya tadapaḥ pṛthivīpate |
pitāmahebhyaśca tathā prīṇayetprapitāmahān ||29||

items.text:
मातामहाय तत्पित्रे तत्पित्रे च समाहितः ।
दद्यात्पैत्रेण तीर्थेन काम्यं चान्यच्छृणुष्व मे ॥३०॥
items.tr:
mātāmahāya tatpitre tatpitre ca samāhitaḥ |
dadyātpaitreṇa tīrthena kāmyaṃ cānyacchṛṇuṣva me ||30||

items.text:
मात्रे प्रमात्रे तन्मात्रे गुरुपत्न्यै तथा नृप ।
गुरूणां मातुलानां च स्निग्धमित्राय भूभुजे ॥३१॥
items.tr:
mātre pramātre tanmātre gurupatnyai tathā nṛpa |
gurūṇāṃ mātulānāṃ ca snigdhamitrāya bhūbhuje ||31||

items.text:
इदं चापि जपेदम्बु दद्यादात्मेच्छया नृप ।
उपकाराय भूतानां कृतदेवादितर्पणम् ॥३२॥
items.tr:
idaṃ cāpi japedambu dadyādātmecchayā nṛpa |
upakārāya bhūtānāṃ kṛtadevāditarpaṇam ||32||

items.text:
देवासुरास्तथा यक्षा नागगन्धर्वराक्षसाः ।
पिशाचा गुह्यकास्सिद्धाः कूष्माण्डाः पशवः खगाः ॥३३॥
items.tr:
devāsurāstathā yakṣā nāgagandharvarākṣasāḥ |
piśācā guhyakāssiddhāḥ kūṣmāṇḍāḥ paśavaḥ khagāḥ ||33||

items.text:
जलेचरा भूनिलया वाय्वाहाराश्च जन्तवः ।
तृप्तिमेतेन यान्त्याशु मद्दत्तेनाम्बुनाऽखिलाः ॥३४॥
items.tr:
jalecarā bhūnilayā vāyvāhārāśca jantavaḥ |
tṛptimetena yāntyāśu maddattenāmbunā'khilāḥ ||34||

items.text:
नरकेषु समस्तेषु यातनासु च संस्थिताः ।
तेषामाप्यायनायैतद्दीयते सलिलं मया ॥३५॥
items.tr:
narakeṣu samasteṣu yātanāsu ca saṃsthitāḥ |
teṣāmāpyāyanāyaitaddīyate salilaṃ mayā ||35||

items.text:
ये बान्धवा बान्धवा ये येऽन्यजन्मनि बान्धवाः ।
ते तृप्तिमखिला यान्तु ये चास्मत्तोयकाङ्क्षिणः ॥३६॥
items.tr:
ye bāndhavā bāndhavā ye ye'nyajanmani bāndhavāḥ |
te tṛptimakhilā yāntu ye cāsmattoyakāṅkṣiṇaḥ ||36||

items.text:
यत्र क्वचनसंस्थानां क्षुत्तृष्णोपहतात्मनाम् ।
इदमाप्यायनायास्तु मया दत्तं तिलोदकम् ॥३७॥
items.tr:
yatra kvacanasaṃsthānāṃ kṣuttṛṣṇopahatātmanām |
idamāpyāyanāyāstu mayā dattaṃ tilodakam ||37||

items.text:
काम्योदकप्रदानं ते मयैतत्कथितं नृप ।
यद्दत्त्वा प्रीणयत्येतन्मनुष्यस्सकलं जगत् ।
जगदाप्यायनोद्भूतं पुण्यमाप्नोति चानघ ॥३८॥
items.tr:
kāmyodakapradānaṃ te mayaitatkathitaṃ nṛpa |
yaddattvā prīṇayatyetanmanuṣyassakalaṃ jagat |
jagadāpyāyanodbhūtaṃ puṇyamāpnoti cānagha ||38||

items.text:
दत्त्वा काम्योदकं सम्यगेतेभ्यः श्राद्धयान्वितः ।
आचम्य च ततो दद्यात्सूर्याय सलिलांजलिम् ॥३९॥
items.tr:
dattvā kāmyodakaṃ samyagetebhyaḥ śrāddhayānvitaḥ |
ācamya ca tato dadyātsūryāya salilāṃjalim ||39||

items.text:
नमो विवस्वते ब्रह्मभास्वते विष्णुतेजसे ।
जगत्सवित्रे शुचये सवित्रे कर्मसाक्षिणे ॥४०॥
items.tr:
namo vivasvate brahmabhāsvate viṣṇutejase |
jagatsavitre śucaye savitre karmasākṣiṇe ||40||

items.text:
ततो गृहाऽर्चनं कुर्यादभीष्टसुरपूजनम् ।
जलाभिषेकैः पुष्पैश्च धूपाद्यैश्च निवेदनम् ॥४१॥
items.tr:
tato gṛhā'rcanaṃ kuryādabhīṣṭasurapūjanam |
jalābhiṣekaiḥ puṣpaiśca dhūpādyaiśca nivedanam ||41||

items.text: अपूर्वमग्निहोत्रं च कुर्यात्प्राग्ब्रह्मणे नृप ॥४२॥
items.tr: apūrvamagnihotraṃ ca kuryātprāgbrahmaṇe nṛpa ||42||

items.text:
प्रजापतिं समुद्दिश्य दद्यादाहुतिमादरात् ।
गृहेभ्यः काश्यपायाथ ततोनुमतये क्रमात् ॥४३॥
items.tr:
prajāpatiṃ samuddiśya dadyādāhutimādarāt |
gṛhebhyaḥ kāśyapāyātha tatonumataye kramāt ||43||

items.text:
तच्छेषं मणिके पृथ्वीपर्जन्येभ्यः क्षिपेत्ततः ।
द्वारे धातुर्विधातुश्च मध्ये च ब्रह्मणे क्षिपेत् ॥४४॥
items.tr:
taccheṣaṃ maṇike pṛthvīparjanyebhyaḥ kṣipettataḥ |
dvāre dhāturvidhātuśca madhye ca brahmaṇe kṣipet ||44||

items.text: गृहस्य पुरषव्याघ्र दिग्देवानपि मे शृणु ॥४५॥
items.tr: gṛhasya puraṣavyāghra digdevānapi me śṛṇu ||45||

items.text:
इंद्रा य धर्मराजाय वरुणाय तथेंदवे ।
प्राच्यादिषु बुधो दद्याद्धुतश्षोआ!त्मकं बलिम् ॥४६॥
items.tr:
iṃdrā ya dharmarājāya varuṇāya tatheṃdave |
prācyādiṣu budho dadyāddhutaśṣoā!tmakaṃ balim ||46||

items.text:
प्रागुत्तरे च दिग्भागे धन्वंतारिबलिं बुधः ।
निर्वपैद्वैश्वदेवं च कर्म कुर्य्यादतः परम् ॥४७॥
items.tr:
prāguttare ca digbhāge dhanvaṃtāribaliṃ budhaḥ |
nirvapaidvaiśvadevaṃ ca karma kuryyādataḥ param ||47||

items.text:
वायव्यां वायवे दिक्षु समस्तासु यथादिशम् ।
ब्रह्मणे चांतरिक्षाय भानवे च क्षिपेद्बलिम् ॥४८॥
items.tr:
vāyavyāṃ vāyave dikṣu samastāsu yathādiśam |
brahmaṇe cāṃtarikṣāya bhānave ca kṣipedbalim ||48||

items.text:
विश्वेदेवान्विश्वभूतानष्टौ विश्वपतीन्पितॄन् ।
यक्षाणां च समुद्दिश्य बलिं दद्यान्नरेश्वर ॥४९॥
items.tr:
viśvedevānviśvabhūtānaṣṭau viśvapatīnpitṝn |
yakṣāṇāṃ ca samuddiśya baliṃ dadyānnareśvara ||49||

items.text:
ततोन्यदन्नमादाय भूमि भागे शुचौ बुधः ।
दद्यादश्षोभूतेभ्यस्स्वेच्छया सुसमाहितः ॥५०॥
items.tr:
tatonyadannamādāya bhūmi bhāge śucau budhaḥ |
dadyādaśṣobhūtebhyassvecchayā susamāhitaḥ ||50||

items.text:
देवा मनुष्याः पशवो वयांसि सिद्धास्सयक्षोरगदैत्यसङ्घाः ।
प्रतोः पिशाचास्तरवस्समस्ता ये चान्नमिच्छन्ति मयात्र दत्तम् ५१ ।
items.tr:
devā manuṣyāḥ paśavo vayāṃsi siddhāssayakṣoragadaityasaṅghāḥ |
pratoḥ piśācāstaravassamastā ye cānnamicchanti mayātra dattam 51 |

items.text:
पिपीलिकाः कीटपतंङ्गकाद्या बुभुक्षिताः कर्मनिबंधबद्धाः ।
प्रयांति ते तृप्तिमिदं मयान्नं तेभ्यो विसृष्टं सुखिनो भवंतु ५२ ।
items.tr:
pipīlikāḥ kīṭapataṃṅgakādyā bubhukṣitāḥ karmanibaṃdhabaddhāḥ |
prayāṃti te tṛptimidaṃ mayānnaṃ tebhyo visṛṣṭaṃ sukhino bhavaṃtu 52 |

items.text:
येषां न माता न पिता न बन्धुर्नैवान्नसिद्धिर्न तथान्नमस्ति ।
तत्तृप्तयेऽन्नं भुवि दत्तमेव ते यान्तु तृप्तिं मुदिता भवन्तु ॥५३॥
items.tr:
yeṣāṃ na mātā na pitā na bandhurnaivānnasiddhirna tathānnamasti |
tattṛptaye'nnaṃ bhuvi dattameva te yāntu tṛptiṃ muditā bhavantu ||53||

items.text:
भूतानि सर्वाणि तथान्नमेतदहं च विष्णुर्न यतोऽन्यदस्ति ।
तस्मादहं भूतनिकायभूतमन्नं प्रयच्छामि भवाय तेषाम् ॥५४॥
items.tr:
bhūtāni sarvāṇi tathānnametadahaṃ ca viṣṇurna yato'nyadasti |
tasmādahaṃ bhūtanikāyabhūtamannaṃ prayacchāmi bhavāya teṣām ||54||

items.text:
चतुर्दशो भूतगणो य एषः तत्र स्थिता येऽखिलभूतसङ्घाः ।
तृप्त्यर्थमन्नं हि मया निसृष्टं तेषामिदं ते मुदिता भवन्तु ॥५५॥
items.tr:
caturdaśo bhūtagaṇo ya eṣaḥ tatra sthitā ye'khilabhūtasaṅghāḥ |
tṛptyarthamannaṃ hi mayā nisṛṣṭaṃ teṣāmidaṃ te muditā bhavantu ||55||

items.text:
इत्युच्चार्य नरो दद्यादन्नं श्रद्धासमन्वितः ।
भुवि सर्वोपकाराय गृही सर्वाश्रयो यतः ॥५६॥
items.tr:
ityuccārya naro dadyādannaṃ śraddhāsamanvitaḥ |
bhuvi sarvopakārāya gṛhī sarvāśrayo yataḥ ||56||

items.text:
श्वचण्डालविहङ्गानां भुवि दद्यान्नरेश्वर ।
ये चान्ये पतिताः केचिदपुत्राः सन्ति मानवाः ॥५७॥
items.tr:
śvacaṇḍālavihaṅgānāṃ bhuvi dadyānnareśvara |
ye cānye patitāḥ kecidaputrāḥ santi mānavāḥ ||57||

items.text:
ततो गोदोहमात्रं वै कालं तिष्ठेद्गृहाङ्गणे ।
अतिथिग्रहणार्थाय तदूर्ध्वं तु यथेच्छया ॥५८॥
items.tr:
tato godohamātraṃ vai kālaṃ tiṣṭhedgṛhāṅgaṇe |
atithigrahaṇārthāya tadūrdhvaṃ tu yathecchayā ||58||

items.text:
अतिथिं तत्र सम्प्राप्तं पूजयेत् स्वागतादिना ।
तथासनप्रदानेन पादप्रक्षालनेन च ॥५९॥
items.tr:
atithiṃ tatra samprāptaṃ pūjayet svāgatādinā |
tathāsanapradānena pādaprakṣālanena ca ||59||

items.text:
श्रद्धया चान्नदानेन प्रियप्रश्नोत्तरेण च ।
गच्छतश्चानुयानेन प्रीतिमुत्पादयेद्गृही ॥६०॥
items.tr:
śraddhayā cānnadānena priyapraśnottareṇa ca |
gacchataścānuyānena prītimutpādayedgṛhī ||60||

items.text:
अज्ञातकुलनामानमन्यदेशादुपागतम् ।
पूजयेदतिथिं सम्यङ्नैकग्रामनिवासिनम् ॥६१॥
items.tr:
ajñātakulanāmānamanyadeśādupāgatam |
pūjayedatithiṃ samyaṅnaikagrāmanivāsinam ||61||

items.text:
अकिञ्चनमसम्बन्धमज्ञातकुलशालिनम् ।
असम्पूज्यातिथिं भुक्त्वा भोक्तुकामं व्रजत्यधः ॥६२॥
items.tr:
akiñcanamasambandhamajñātakulaśālinam |
asampūjyātithiṃ bhuktvā bhoktukāmaṃ vrajatyadhaḥ ||62||

items.text:
स्वाध्यायगोत्राचरणमपृष्ट्वा च तथा कुलम् ।
हिरण्यगर्भबुद्ध्या तं मन्येताभ्यागतं गृही ॥६३॥
items.tr:
svādhyāyagotrācaraṇamapṛṣṭvā ca tathā kulam |
hiraṇyagarbhabuddhyā taṃ manyetābhyāgataṃ gṛhī ||63||

items.text:
पित्रर्थं चापरं विप्रमेकमप्याशयेन्नृप ।
तद्देश्यं विदिताचारसम्भूतिं पाञ्चयज्ञिकम् ॥६४॥
items.tr:
pitrarthaṃ cāparaṃ vipramekamapyāśayennṛpa |
taddeśyaṃ viditācārasambhūtiṃ pāñcayajñikam ||64||

items.text:
अन्नाग्रं च समुद्धृत्य हन्तकारोपकल्पितम् ।
निर्वापभूतं भूपाल श्रोत्रियायोपपादयेत् ॥६५॥
items.tr:
annāgraṃ ca samuddhṛtya hantakāropakalpitam |
nirvāpabhūtaṃ bhūpāla śrotriyāyopapādayet ||65||

items.text:
दद्याच्च भिक्षात्रितयं परिव्राड्ब्रह्मचारिणाम् ।
इच्छया च बुधो दद्याद्विभवे सत्यवारितम् ॥६६॥
items.tr:
dadyācca bhikṣātritayaṃ parivrāḍbrahmacāriṇām |
icchayā ca budho dadyādvibhave satyavāritam ||66||

items.text:
इत्येतेऽतिथयः प्रोक्ता प्रागुक्ता भिक्षवश्च ये ।
चतुरः पूजयित्वैतान्नृप पापात् प्रमुच्यते ॥६७॥
items.tr:
ityete'tithayaḥ proktā prāguktā bhikṣavaśca ye |
caturaḥ pūjayitvaitānnṛpa pāpāt pramucyate ||67||

items.text:
अतिथिर्यस्य भग्नाशो गृहात् प्रतिनिवर्त्तते ।
स तस्मै दुष्कृतं दत्त्वा पुण्यमादाय गच्छति ॥६८॥
items.tr:
atithiryasya bhagnāśo gṛhāt pratinivarttate |
sa tasmai duṣkṛtaṃ dattvā puṇyamādāya gacchati ||68||

items.text:
धाता प्रजापतिः शक्रो वह्निर्वसुगणोऽर्यमा ।
प्रविश्यातिथिमेते वै भुञ्जन्तेऽन्नं नरेश्वर ॥६९॥
items.tr:
dhātā prajāpatiḥ śakro vahnirvasugaṇo'ryamā |
praviśyātithimete vai bhuñjante'nnaṃ nareśvara ||69||

items.text:
तस्मादतिथिपूजायां यतेत सततं नरः ।
स केवलमघं भुङ्क्ते यो भुङ्क्ते ह्यतिथिं विना ॥७०॥
items.tr:
tasmādatithipūjāyāṃ yateta satataṃ naraḥ |
sa kevalamaghaṃ bhuṅkte yo bhuṅkte hyatithiṃ vinā ||70||

items.text:
ततः सुवासिनीदुःखिगर्भिणीवृद्धबालकान् ।
भोजयेत् संस्कृतान्नेन प्रथमं चरमं गृही ॥७१॥
items.tr:
tataḥ suvāsinīduḥkhigarbhiṇīvṛddhabālakān |
bhojayet saṃskṛtānnena prathamaṃ caramaṃ gṛhī ||71||

items.text:
अभुक्तवत्सु चैतेषु भुञ्जन् भुङ्क्ते स दुष्कृतम् ।
मृतश्च गत्वा नरकं श्लेष्मभुग्जायते नरः ॥७२॥
items.tr:
abhuktavatsu caiteṣu bhuñjan bhuṅkte sa duṣkṛtam |
mṛtaśca gatvā narakaṃ śleṣmabhugjāyate naraḥ ||72||

items.text:
अस्नाताशी मलं भुङ्क्ते ह्यजपी पूयशोणितम् ।
असंस्कृतान्नभुङ्मूत्रं बालादिप्रथमं शकृत् ॥७३॥
items.tr:
asnātāśī malaṃ bhuṅkte hyajapī pūyaśoṇitam |
asaṃskṛtānnabhuṅmūtraṃ bālādiprathamaṃ śakṛt ||73||

items.text: अहोमी च कृमीन् भुङ्क्ते अदत्त्वा विषमश्नुते ॥७४॥
items.tr: ahomī ca kṛmīn bhuṅkte adattvā viṣamaśnute ||74||

items.text:
तस्माच्छृणुष्व राजेन्द्र यथा भुञ्जीत वै गृही ।
भुञ्जतश्च यथा पुंसः पापबन्धो न जायते ॥७५॥
items.tr:
tasmācchṛṇuṣva rājendra yathā bhuñjīta vai gṛhī |
bhuñjataśca yathā puṃsaḥ pāpabandho na jāyate ||75||

items.text:
इह चारोग्यविपुलं बलबुद्धिस्तथा नृप ।
भवत्यरिष्टशान्तिश्च वैरिपक्षाभिचारिणः ॥७६॥
items.tr:
iha cārogyavipulaṃ balabuddhistathā nṛpa |
bhavatyariṣṭaśāntiśca vairipakṣābhicāriṇaḥ ||76||

items.text:
स्नातो यथावत् कृत्वा च देवर्षिपितृतर्पणम् ।
प्रशस्तरत्नपाणिस्तु भुञ्जीत प्रयतो गृही ॥७७॥
items.tr:
snāto yathāvat kṛtvā ca devarṣipitṛtarpaṇam |
praśastaratnapāṇistu bhuñjīta prayato gṛhī ||77||

items.text:
कृते जपे हुते वह्नौ शुद्धवस्त्रधरो नृप ।
दत्त्वाऽतिथिभ्यो विप्रेभ्यो गुरुभ्यस्संश्रिताय च ।
पुण्यगन्धधरः शस्तमाल्यधारी नरेश्वर ॥७८॥
items.tr:
kṛte jape hute vahnau śuddhavastradharo nṛpa |
dattvā'tithibhyo viprebhyo gurubhyassaṃśritāya ca |
puṇyagandhadharaḥ śastamālyadhārī nareśvara ||78||

items.text:
नैकवस्त्रधरो नार्द्रपाणिपादो महीपते ।
विशुद्धवदनः प्रीतो भुञ्जीत न विदिङ्मुखः ॥७९॥
items.tr:
naikavastradharo nārdrapāṇipādo mahīpate |
viśuddhavadanaḥ prīto bhuñjīta na vidiṅmukhaḥ ||79||

items.text:
प्राङ्मुखोदङ्मुखो वापि न चैवान्यमना नरः ।
अन्नं प्रशस्तं पथ्यं च प्रोक्षितं प्रोक्षणोदकैः ॥८०॥
items.tr:
prāṅmukhodaṅmukho vāpi na caivānyamanā naraḥ |
annaṃ praśastaṃ pathyaṃ ca prokṣitaṃ prokṣaṇodakaiḥ ||80||

items.text:
न कुत्सिताहृतं नैव जुगुप्सापदसंस्कृतम् ।
दत्त्वा तु भक्तं शिष्येभ्यः क्षुधितेभ्यस्तथा गृही ॥८१॥
items.tr:
na kutsitāhṛtaṃ naiva jugupsāpadasaṃskṛtam |
dattvā tu bhaktaṃ śiṣyebhyaḥ kṣudhitebhyastathā gṛhī ||81||

items.text: प्रशस्तशुद्धपात्रे तु भुञ्जीताकुपितो द्विजः ॥८२॥
items.tr: praśastaśuddhapātre tu bhuñjītākupito dvijaḥ ||82||

items.text:
नासन्दिसंस्थिते पात्रे नादेशे च नरेश्वर ।
नाकाले नातिसङ्कीर्णे दत्त्वाग्रं च नरोऽग्नये ॥८३॥
items.tr:
nāsandisaṃsthite pātre nādeśe ca nareśvara |
nākāle nātisaṅkīrṇe dattvāgraṃ ca naro'gnaye ||83||

items.text:
मन्त्राभिमन्त्रितं शस्तं न च पर्युषितं नृप ।
अन्यत्र फलमूलेभ्यः शुष्कशाखादिकात् तथा ॥८४॥
items.tr:
mantrābhimantritaṃ śastaṃ na ca paryuṣitaṃ nṛpa |
anyatra phalamūlebhyaḥ śuṣkaśākhādikāt tathā ||84||

items.text:
तद्वद्धारीतकेभ्यश्च गुडभक्ष्येभ्य एव च ।
भुञ्जीतोद्धृतसाराणि न कदापि नरेश्वर ॥८५॥
items.tr:
tadvaddhārītakebhyaśca guḍabhakṣyebhya eva ca |
bhuñjītoddhṛtasārāṇi na kadāpi nareśvara ||85||

items.text:
न शेषं पुरुषोऽश्नीयादन्यत्र जगतीपते ।
मध्वम्बुदधिसर्पिभ्यः सक्तुभ्यश्च विवेकवान् ॥८६॥
items.tr:
na śeṣaṃ puruṣo'śnīyādanyatra jagatīpate |
madhvambudadhisarpibhyaḥ saktubhyaśca vivekavān ||86||

items.text:
अश्नीयात् तन्मयो भूत्वा पूर्वं तु मधुरं रसम् ।
लवणाम्लौ तथा मध्ये कटुतिक्तादिकांस्ततः ॥८७॥
items.tr:
aśnīyāt tanmayo bhūtvā pūrvaṃ tu madhuraṃ rasam |
lavaṇāmlau tathā madhye kaṭutiktādikāṃstataḥ ||87||

items.text:
प्राग्द्रवं पुरुषोऽश्नीयान्मध्ये कठिनभोजनः ।
अन्ते पुनर्द्रवाशी तु बलारोग्ये न मुञ्चति ॥८८॥
items.tr:
prāgdravaṃ puruṣo'śnīyānmadhye kaṭhinabhojanaḥ |
ante punardravāśī tu balārogye na muñcati ||88||

items.text:
अनिन्द्यं भक्षयेदित्थं वाग्यतोऽन्नमकुत्सयन् ।
पञ्चग्रासं महामौनं प्राणाद्याप्यायनं हि तत् ॥८९॥
items.tr:
anindyaṃ bhakṣayeditthaṃ vāgyato'nnamakutsayan |
pañcagrāsaṃ mahāmaunaṃ prāṇādyāpyāyanaṃ hi tat ||89||

items.text:
भुक्त्वा सम्यगथाचम्य प्राङ्मुखोदङ्मुखोऽपि वा ।
यथावत् पुनराचामेत् पाणी प्रक्षाल्य मूलतः ॥९०॥
items.tr:
bhuktvā samyagathācamya prāṅmukhodaṅmukho'pi vā |
yathāvat punarācāmet pāṇī prakṣālya mūlataḥ ||90||

items.text:
स्वस्थः प्रशान्तचित्तस्तु कृतासनपरिग्रहः ।
अभीष्टदेवतानां तु कुर्वीत स्मरणं नरः ॥९१॥
items.tr:
svasthaḥ praśāntacittastu kṛtāsanaparigrahaḥ |
abhīṣṭadevatānāṃ tu kurvīta smaraṇaṃ naraḥ ||91||

items.text:
अग्निराप्याययेद्धातुं पार्थिवं पवनेरितः ।
दत्तावकाशं नभसा जरयत्यस्तु मे सुखम् ॥९२॥
items.tr:
agnirāpyāyayeddhātuṃ pārthivaṃ pavaneritaḥ |
dattāvakāśaṃ nabhasā jarayatyastu me sukham ||92||

items.text:
अन्नं बलाय मे भूमेरपामग्न्यनिलस्य च ।
भवत्येतत्परीणतं ममास्त्यव्याहतं सुखम् ॥९३॥
items.tr:
annaṃ balāya me bhūmerapāmagnyanilasya ca |
bhavatyetatparīṇataṃ mamāstyavyāhataṃ sukham ||93||

items.text:
प्राणापानसमानानामुदानव्यानयोस्तथा ।
अन्नं पुष्टिकरं चास्तु ममाप्यव्याहतं सुखम् ॥९४॥
items.tr:
prāṇāpānasamānānāmudānavyānayostathā |
annaṃ puṣṭikaraṃ cāstu mamāpyavyāhataṃ sukham ||94||

items.text:
अगस्तिरग्निर्वडवानलश्च भुक्तं मयान्नं जरयत्वशेषम् ।
सुखं च मे तत्परिणामसम्भवं यच्छन्त्वरोगं मम चास्तु देहे ॥९५॥
items.tr:
agastiragnirvaḍavānalaśca bhuktaṃ mayānnaṃ jarayatvaśeṣam |
sukhaṃ ca me tatpariṇāmasambhavaṃ yacchantvarogaṃ mama cāstu dehe ||95||

items.text:
विष्णुः समस्तेन्द्रियदेहदेही वृथा न भूतो भगवान् यथैकः ।
सत्येन तेनात्तमशेषमन्नमारोग्यतां मे परिणाममेतु ॥९६॥
items.tr:
viṣṇuḥ samastendriyadehadehī vṛthā na bhūto bhagavān yathaikaḥ |
satyena tenāttamaśeṣamannamārogyatāṃ me pariṇāmametu ||96||

items.text:
विष्णुरत्ता तथैवान्नं परिणामश्च वै तथा ।
सत्येन तेन मद्भुक्तं जीर्यत्यन्नमिदं तथा ॥९७॥
items.tr:
viṣṇurattā tathaivānnaṃ pariṇāmaśca vai tathā |
satyena tena madbhuktaṃ jīryatyannamidaṃ tathā ||97||

items.text:
इत्युच्चार्य स्वहस्तेन परिमृज्य तथोदरम् ।
अनायासप्रदायीनि कुर्यात् कर्माण्यतन्द्रितः ॥९८॥
items.tr:
ityuccārya svahastena parimṛjya tathodaram |
anāyāsapradāyīni kuryāt karmāṇyatandritaḥ ||98||

items.text:
सच्छास्त्रादिविनोदेन सन्मार्गादविरोधिना ।
दिनं नयेत् ततस्सन्ध्यामुपतिष्ठेत् समाहितः ॥९९॥
items.tr:
sacchāstrādivinodena sanmārgādavirodhinā |
dinaṃ nayet tatassandhyāmupatiṣṭhet samāhitaḥ ||99||

items.text:
दिनान्तसन्ध्यां सूर्येण पूर्वामृक्षैर्युतां बुधः ।
उपतिष्ठेद्यथान्याय्यं सम्यगाचम्य पार्थिव ॥१००॥
items.tr:
dināntasandhyāṃ sūryeṇa pūrvāmṛkṣairyutāṃ budhaḥ |
upatiṣṭhedyathānyāyyaṃ samyagācamya pārthiva ||100||

items.text:
सर्वकालमुपस्थानं सन्ध्ययोः पार्थिवेष्यते ।
अन्यत्र सूतकाशौचविभ्रमातुरभीतितः ॥१०१।
सूर्येणाभ्युदितो यश्च त्यक्तः सूर्येण वा स्वपन् ।
अन्यत्रातुरभावात्तु प्रायश्चित्ती भवेन्नरः ॥१०२॥
items.tr:
sarvakālamupasthānaṃ sandhyayoḥ pārthiveṣyate |
anyatra sūtakāśaucavibhramāturabhītitaḥ ||101|
sūryeṇābhyudito yaśca tyaktaḥ sūryeṇa vā svapan |
anyatrāturabhāvāttu prāyaścittī bhavennaraḥ ||102||

items.text:
तस्मादनुदिते सूर्ये समुत्थाय महीपते ।
उपतिष्ठेन्नरस्सन्ध्यामस्वपंश्च दिनान्तजाम् ॥१०३॥
items.tr:
tasmādanudite sūrye samutthāya mahīpate |
upatiṣṭhennarassandhyāmasvapaṃśca dināntajām ||103||

items.text:
उपतिष्ठन्ति वै सन्ध्यां ये न पूर्वां न पश्चिमाम् ।
व्रजन्ति ते दुरात्मानस्तमिस्रं नरकं नृप ॥१०४॥
items.tr:
upatiṣṭhanti vai sandhyāṃ ye na pūrvāṃ na paścimām |
vrajanti te durātmānastamisraṃ narakaṃ nṛpa ||104||

items.text:
पुनः पाकमुपादाय सायमप्यवनीपते ।
वैश्वदेवनिमित्तं वै पत्न्यमन्त्रं बलिं हरेत् ॥१०५॥
items.tr:
punaḥ pākamupādāya sāyamapyavanīpate |
vaiśvadevanimittaṃ vai patnyamantraṃ baliṃ haret ||105||

items.text: तत्रापि श्वपचादिभ्यस्तथैवान्नविसर्जनम् ॥१०६॥
items.tr: tatrāpi śvapacādibhyastathaivānnavisarjanam ||106||

items.text:
अतिथिं चागतं तत्र स्वशक्तया पूजयेद्बुधः ।
पादशौचासनप्रह्वस्वागतोक्त्या च पूजनम् ।
ततश्चान्नप्रदानेन शयनेन च पार्थिव ॥१०७॥
items.tr:
atithiṃ cāgataṃ tatra svaśaktayā pūjayedbudhaḥ |
pādaśaucāsanaprahvasvāgatoktyā ca pūjanam |
tataścānnapradānena śayanena ca pārthiva ||107||

items.text:
दिवातिथौ तु विमुखे गते यत्पातकं नृप ।
तदेवाष्टगुणं पुंसस्सूर्योढे विमुखे गते ॥१०८॥
items.tr:
divātithau tu vimukhe gate yatpātakaṃ nṛpa |
tadevāṣṭaguṇaṃ puṃsassūryoḍhe vimukhe gate ||108||

items.text:
तस्मात् स्वशक्त्या राजेन्द्र सूर्योढमतिथिं नरः ।
पूजयेत् पूजिते तस्मिन् पूजितास्सर्वदेवताः ॥१०९॥
items.tr:
tasmāt svaśaktyā rājendra sūryoḍhamatithiṃ naraḥ |
pūjayet pūjite tasmin pūjitāssarvadevatāḥ ||109||

items.text:
अन्नशाकाम्बुदानेन स्वशक्त्या पूजयेत् पुमान् ।
शयनप्रस्तरमहीप्रदानैरथवापि तम् ॥११०॥
items.tr:
annaśākāmbudānena svaśaktyā pūjayet pumān |
śayanaprastaramahīpradānairathavāpi tam ||110||

items.text:
कृतपादादिशौचस्तु भुक्त्वा सायं ततो गृही ।
गच्छेच्छय्यामस्फुटितामपि दारुमयीं नृप ॥१११॥
items.tr:
kṛtapādādiśaucastu bhuktvā sāyaṃ tato gṛhī |
gacchecchayyāmasphuṭitāmapi dārumayīṃ nṛpa ||111||

items.text:
नाविशालां न वै भुग्नां नासमां मलिनां न च ।
न च जन्तुमयीं शय्यामधितिष्ठेदनास्तृताम् ॥११२॥
items.tr:
nāviśālāṃ na vai bhugnāṃ nāsamāṃ malināṃ na ca |
na ca jantumayīṃ śayyāmadhitiṣṭhedanāstṛtām ||112||

items.text:
प्राच्यां दिशि शिरश्शस्तं याम्यायामथ वा नृप ।
सदैव स्वपतः पुंसो विपरीतं तु रोगदम् ॥११३॥
items.tr:
prācyāṃ diśi śiraśśastaṃ yāmyāyāmatha vā nṛpa |
sadaiva svapataḥ puṃso viparītaṃ tu rogadam ||113||

items.text:
ऋतावुपगमश्शस्तस्स्वपत्न्यामवनीपते ।
पुन्नामर्क्षे शुभे काले ज्येष्ठायुग्मासु रात्रिषु ॥११४॥
items.tr:
ṛtāvupagamaśśastassvapatnyāmavanīpate |
punnāmarkṣe śubhe kāle jyeṣṭhāyugmāsu rātriṣu ||114||

items.text:
नाद्यूनां तु स्त्रियं गच्छेन्नातुरां न रजस्वलाम् ।
नानिष्टां न प्रकुपितां न त्रस्तां न च गर्भिणीम् ॥११५॥
items.tr:
nādyūnāṃ tu striyaṃ gacchennāturāṃ na rajasvalām |
nāniṣṭāṃ na prakupitāṃ na trastāṃ na ca garbhiṇīm ||115||

items.text:
नादक्षिणां नान्यकामां नाकामां नान्ययोषितम् ।
क्षुत्क्षामां नातिभुक्तां वा स्वयं चैभिर्गुणैर्युतः ॥११६॥
items.tr:
nādakṣiṇāṃ nānyakāmāṃ nākāmāṃ nānyayoṣitam |
kṣutkṣāmāṃ nātibhuktāṃ vā svayaṃ caibhirguṇairyutaḥ ||116||

items.text:
स्नातस्स्रग्गन्धधृक् प्रीतो नाध्मातः क्षुधितोऽपि वा ।
सकामस्सानुरागश्च व्यवायं पुरुषो व्रजेत् ॥११७॥
items.tr:
snātassraggandhadhṛk prīto nādhmātaḥ kṣudhito'pi vā |
sakāmassānurāgaśca vyavāyaṃ puruṣo vrajet ||117||

items.text:
चतुर्दश्यष्टमी चैव तथामा चाथ पूर्णिमा ।
पर्वाण्येतानि राजेन्द्र रविसङ्क्रान्तिरेव च ॥११८॥
items.tr:
caturdaśyaṣṭamī caiva tathāmā cātha pūrṇimā |
parvāṇyetāni rājendra ravisaṅkrāntireva ca ||118||

items.text:
तैलस्त्रीमांससम्भोगी सर्वेष्वेतेषु वै पुमान् ।
विण्मूत्रभोजनं नाम प्रयाति नरकं मृतः ॥११९॥
items.tr:
tailastrīmāṃsasambhogī sarveṣveteṣu vai pumān |
viṇmūtrabhojanaṃ nāma prayāti narakaṃ mṛtaḥ ||119||

items.text:
अशेषपर्वस्वेतेषु तस्मात् संयमिभिर्बुधैः ।
भाव्यं सच्छास्त्रदेवेज्याध्यानजप्यपरैर्नरैः ॥१२०॥
items.tr:
aśeṣaparvasveteṣu tasmāt saṃyamibhirbudhaiḥ |
bhāvyaṃ sacchāstradevejyādhyānajapyaparairnaraiḥ ||120||

items.text:
नान्ययोनावयोनौ वा नोपयुक्तौषधस्तथा ।
द्विजदेवगुरूणां च व्यवायी नाश्रमे भवेत् ॥१२१॥
items.tr:
nānyayonāvayonau vā nopayuktauṣadhastathā |
dvijadevagurūṇāṃ ca vyavāyī nāśrame bhavet ||121||

items.text:
चैत्यचत्वरतीरेषु नैव गोष्ठे चतुष्पथे ।
नैव श्मशानोपवने सलिलेषु महीपते ॥१२२॥
items.tr:
caityacatvaratīreṣu naiva goṣṭhe catuṣpathe |
naiva śmaśānopavane salileṣu mahīpate ||122||

items.text:
प्रोक्तपर्वस्वशेषेषु नैव भूपाल सन्ध्ययोः ।
गच्छेद्व्यवायं मनसा न मूत्रोच्चारपीडितः ॥१२३॥
items.tr:
proktaparvasvaśeṣeṣu naiva bhūpāla sandhyayoḥ |
gacchedvyavāyaṃ manasā na mūtroccārapīḍitaḥ ||123||

items.text:
पर्वस्वभिगमोऽधन्यो दिवा पापप्रदो नृप ।
भुवि रोगावहो नॄणामप्रशस्तो जलाशये ॥१२४॥
items.tr:
parvasvabhigamo'dhanyo divā pāpaprado nṛpa |
bhuvi rogāvaho nṝṇāmapraśasto jalāśaye ||124||

items.text:
परदारान्न गच्छेत मनसापि कथञ्चन ।
किमु वाचास्थिबन्धोऽपि नास्ति तेषु व्यवायिनाम् ॥१२५॥
items.tr:
paradārānna gaccheta manasāpi kathañcana |
kimu vācāsthibandho'pi nāsti teṣu vyavāyinām ||125||

items.text:
मृतो नरकमभ्येति हीयतेऽत्रापि चायुषः ।
परदाररतिः पुंसामिह चामुत्र भीतिदा ॥१२६॥
items.tr:
mṛto narakamabhyeti hīyate'trāpi cāyuṣaḥ |
paradāraratiḥ puṃsāmiha cāmutra bhītidā ||126||

items.text:
इति मत्वा स्वदारेषु ऋतुमत्सु बुधो व्रजेत् ।
यथोक्तदोषहीनेषु सकामेष्वनृतावपि ॥१२७॥
items.tr:
iti matvā svadāreṣu ṛtumatsu budho vrajet |
yathoktadoṣahīneṣu sakāmeṣvanṛtāvapi ||127||

en_chapter: Sagara said—"O Muni, I wish to hear from you of such religious observances, performing which a householder does not meet with the wane of piety either in this world or in the next".

Aurva said—"Hear, O lord of earth, an account of all those religious observances celebrating which a man conquers both this and the next world. The term sat means Sādhu; and they are called Sādhus or saints who are freed from all blemishes. And their practices are called Sāddhachāras. O lord of earth, the seven Rishis, the Manus and the Patriarchs are those who have laid down and observed those practices. Let the wise, O king, get up at Brahmā Muhartta, when the mind is at rest, meditate upon virtue and wealth not incompatible with the former. He should also meditate upon desire not conflicting with the other two. And he must equally meditate upon the three ends of life for the purpose of counteracting the unseen consequences of good or best acts. He should renounce, O king, such wealth and desire as stand in the way of virtue, and he should abstain from such religious acts as give uneasiness, and as are not compatible with the rules of society. O lord of men, having got up from bed early in the morning, he must offer adoration to the sun and then proceeding to the South-East quarter at a distance of a bow-shot or more, or somewhere remote from the village he must void the impurities of nature. A man should not void the impurities of nature either in the court yard of his house or in any place where is the print of a man's foot. The wise should not pass urine either on his own shadow, nor on the shadow of a tree, nor on a cow, nor against the sun nor on fire, nor against the wind, nor on spiritual preceptor, nor men of the first three castes. Nor he should pass excrement in a ploughed field, or a pasturage, or in the company of men, or on a high road, or in rivers and the like which are holy, or on the bank of a river or in a cremation ground. O king, the wise should pass urine with his face towards the north during the day and towards the south during the night. While passing excrement he should spread grass on the earth and cover his head with cloth and should not wait there long, and should not speak during that time. To clean his hand he should not take earth from an ant-hill, not a rat-hole, nor from water, nor from what has been left after being used for that purpose, nor from what has been used to plaster a cottage, nor that which has been thrown up by insects, or turned over by the plough. He must avoid all these kinds of earth for the purpose of cleanliness; he should use one handful after passing urine, three handfuls after passing excrement, ten handfuls are to be rubbed over the left hand and seven on both hands. He should then rinse his mouth with pure water which is neither fetid, nor frothy nor full of bubbles. After that, he should, being composed, use earth to cleanse his feet, washing them well with water.

"He must then drink water thrice and wash his face twice with it and then touch with his head, the cavities of the eyes, ears and nostrils, the forehead, navel and the heart. Having finally washed his mouth he must clean and arrange his hairs and must decorate his body, before a looking glass with unguents, garlands and perfumes. He, then according to the practice of his caste, should earn money for maintenance and should worship the deities with firm faith. Sacrifices with acid juice, those with clarified butter and those with offerings of food, may be performed with wealth; therefore men should endeavour much to acquire wealth.

"For performing daily devotional rites a man should bathe in the water of a river, a natural channel, or a mountain torrent or he should bathe on a dry ground with the water drawn from well or he should bring that water to his house if he had any objection to bathing on the spot. Bathed and clad in clean clothes, he should, with concentrated mind offer oblations to the manes and Rishis with that water. He should offer water thrice for the satisfaction of the celestials, thrice for the satisfaction of the Rishis and once for the patriarchs. He should make three libations for the satisfaction of the manes. He should, with the part of the hand sacred to the manes, offer wafer to his paternal grand father, great grand father, maternal grand father, great grand father and his father, and according to his pleasure to his own mother and his mother's mother and grand mother, to the wife of his preceptor, to his preceptor, his maternal uncle, and other relations, to a dear friend and to the king. He should then, O king, offer water to the celestials for the benefit of all animals, reciting the prayer. 'May the celestials, demons, Yakshas, Serpents, Rākshasas, Gandharvas, Pisāchas, Guhyakas, Siddas, Kushmandas, trees, birds, fish, all that inhabit the waters or the earth, or the air, be propitiated by the water I have offered to them. This water is presented by me for the mitigation of the sufferings of all those who have been put to hell. Let them be propitiated with this water who are my friends, who are not my friends, who were my friends in my former birth and all those who expect water from me. May this water and sesamum offered by me remove the hunger and thirst of all those who are suffering therefrom wherever they may live'. The offerings, of water, O king, in the manner I have described, give satisfaction to all the world. Having offered water duly and reverentially to all the sinless man obtains the piety that comes from satisfying the world.

"Having rinsed his mouth he must offer water to the sun touching his forehead with folded hands and reciting the following player—'Salutation to the radiant Vaivaswat—the effulgence of Vishnu; to the pure illuminator of the universe; to Sāvitri, the giver of fruits for all actions'. He must then go through the family worship, offering water, flowers, and incense to the tutelary deity. He must then offer oblations to fire, first invoking Brahmā then Prajāpati. He must then offer water to Guhya, Kāshyapa and Anumati in succession and then offer the remainder to the earth, to water and to rain in a pitcher at hand. O foremost of men, he must offer water to Dhātri Vidhātri at the doors of his house and to Brahmā in the middle of it. Hear from me how he should then worship the deities presiding over the various quarters.

"He should offer the Bali containing the remaining portions of the oblations to Indra, Yama, Varuna and Soma on the four sides of his house. And in the north-east quarter the wise should offer it to Dhanwantari; then he should offer the remaining portion to Viswadevas, then in the north-east to wind then in all directions to the cardinal points, to Brahmā, to the atmosphere, and to the sun, to all the celestials, to all beings, to the lords of beings, to the manes, and to Yakshas. Thereupon taking other rice the learned should cast it on a clean spot of ground as an offering to all beings and with a collected mind should repeat the following prayer—'May celestials, men, animals, birds, saints. Yakshas, serpents, demons, ghosts, goblins, trees and all those who desire food from me; may ants, worms, moths and other insects who are hungry and chained in acts, obtain satisfaction from food offered by me and enjoy bliss. I offer this food on the ground for them who have got no mother, no father, no friends, no food, nor the means for preparing it. May they be satisfied with the food offered for their satisfaction. All these animals, this food and myself are at one with Vishnu—for there exists nothing but Vishnu; I am not different from all beings, and therefore for their sustenance I offer this food. May all beings, that belong to the fourteen orders of existent things, be satisfied and delighted with the food offered by me'.

"Having repeated this prayer the householder should devoutly throw the food on the ground for the benefit of all beings; for the householder is thence the supporter of them all. He should also disperse food on the ground for dogs, outcasts, birds and all mean and degraded persons.

"Thereupon to receive guests the householder should wait in the courtyard of his house as long as it takes to milch a cow or for a longer period if he pleases. If a guest comes he must be received with all hospitality; he must be offered a seat, his feet are to be washed, food should be respectfully given to him, he must be spoken to with all kindness and civility and when he goes away, the friendly wishes of the host must accompany him. The householder should pay attention to that guest who comes from another place and whose lineage is not known. He should not make him a guest who is an inhabitant of the same village. He who feeds himself, neglecting a guest, who is poor, who is not his relation, who comes from another place and is desirous of eating, goes to hell. The householder should receive his guest regarding him as the golden embryo without inquiring his studies, his schools, his practices or his race.

"A householder, O king, at the Srādha ceremony of his father, should feed another Brāhmin, who is of the same village, whose pedigree and practices are known and who performs the five sacramental rites. He should also present to a Brāhmin, who is well versed in the Vedas, four handfuls of food, set apart, with the exclamation Hanta. If he has got means left after making these three sorts of gifts, the learned should, according to his pleasure, make gifts to a mendicant and a religious student. These three, with the addition of the mendicant described before, are to be considered as guests; and he, who treats these four sorts of persons with hospitality, is freed of the debt due to his fellow beings. The guest, who goes elsewhere disappointed from any house, transfers his own sins to the owner of the house and takes away the house-holder's merits. Brahmā, Prajāpati, Indra, fire, the Vasus, the sun are present in the person of a guest and share the food that is offered to him. Therefore a man should assiduously satisfy the duties of hospitality; for a man, who eats his food without giving any to his guest, feeds only upon his own sin. Thereupon the householder must satisfy with well-seasoned food the damsel living in her father's house, those who are ill, the pregnant woman, the aged and the infants of the house and then he should eat himself. The householder, who eats his food without feeding these, feeds upon his own iniquity and after his death is condemned in hell to feed upon phlegm. He, who eats, without performing ablutions, feeds upon filth; he, who eats without repeating his prayers, feeds upon matter and blood; he, who eats unconsecrated food, drinks urine; and he, who eats before the infants and the aged are fed, is doomed in hell to live upon ordure. O foremost of kings, I shall now describe, do you hear, how a householder should eat and for which he would not be sullied with iniquity, his perpetual health and increased vigour would be secured and all evils and hostilities would be averted. Having bathed and offered duly libations to the celestials, Rishis, and manes and adorned his hand with precious jewels, having recited introductory prayers, offered oblations with fire, food to guests, to Brāhmans, to his elders and to his family, the householder should take his meal, wearing unsullied cloth, excellent garlands and sprinkled with perfumes. He must not eat, O lord, of men, with a single garment on, nor with wet hands and feet.

"He must not eat with his face directed to my intermediate point of horizon, but facing the east or the north; and with a smiling countenance, happy and attentive, let him take good and wholesome food boiled with clean water, procured from no mean person, nor by improper means nor improperly cooked. Having given a part to his hungry companions he should take food without reproach from a clean, handsome vessels which must not be placed upon a low stool or bed. He must not take his food in an unbecoming place or out of season or in an unsuitable mood, giving the first morsel to fire. His food, O king, must be consecrated with suitable texts, must be good and must not be stale except in the case of fruit or meat. Nor it should be made of dry vegetable substances other than jujubes or preparation of molasses. And a man should never eat that of which the juices have been extracted. Nor a man should so eat as nothing will be left of his meal except in the case of flour, cakes, honey, water, curds and butter. He should with a devoted mind first taste that which has good flavour; in the middle he should take salt and sour things and in the end he should take those which are pungent and bitter. The person, who begins his food with fluid things, takes solid food in the middle and finishes with fluid things, will ever be strong and healthy. In this wise he should take such food as is not prohibited, should be silent at the time of eating and should take five handfuls for the nutriment of the vital principle. After he has taken his food, he should, facing the east or the north, rinse his mouth, and having washed his hands up to the wrist he should again sip water. Then with a satisfied and calm mind he should take his seat, meditate upon his tutelary deity and pray 'May fire excited by air cause this food to digest in the space afforded by the etherial atmosphere, convert this into the earthly elements of this body and give me satisfaction. May this food, when assimilated, contribute to the vigour of the earth, water, fire, and air of my body and afford unmixed satisfaction. May Agasti, Agni and submarine fire bring about the digestion of the food I have taken and may I enjoy happiness consequent thereupon and may my body be freed from all ills. May Vishnu, who is the chief principle of all senses, of all bodies and souls, be propitiated with my faith and may cause such assimilation the food I have eaten as may invigorate my health. Verily Vishnu is the eater, the food and the nourishment, may the food I have taken, through this faith, be digested'.

"Having recited this prayer he should rub his stomach with his hand, and renouncing idleness should engage in such action as can easily he performed. He should spend the day in the reading of sacred writings and in such amusements as are authorized by the righteous and when the Sandhya sets in he must engage in devotion. O king, he must perform the morning rites before the stars have disappeared and perform the evening rites before the sun has quite set. The morning and evening rites should never be neglected except at seasons of impurity, anxiety, sickness or alarm. He, who but for illness lies on bed at the hours of sunrise and sunset, is guilty of iniquity. Therefore a man should rise before the sun in the morning and sleep not until after he has set. Those, who sinfully neglect the performance of both the morning and evening rites, go to the hell of darkness after death. And having prepared food in the evening, the wife, of the householder with a view to obtain the fruit of the Viçwadeva rite, should give food, without offering any prayers, to outcasts or unclean persons. The householder, as his means allow, should again show hospitality to any guest who may come receiving him with the salutation of evening and offering him water to wash his feet, a seat, a supper and a bed. The sin, consequent upon not receiving hospitably a guest who comes after sunset, is eight times greater than that of turning away one who comes during the day. A person should therefore particularly show respect to him who seeks refuge after sunset, for the respect, given to his satisfaction, will afford pleasure to all the celestials. The householder should, therefore, as his means permit him, give a guest food, potherbs, water, a bed, a mat, or if he cannot give any thing more, ground only on which to lie.

"Having taken his evening meal and washed his feet a householder should take rest. His bed must be complete and made of wood, it must have ample space, must not be cracked nor uneven, nor dirty nor infested by insects and must have a bedding. The householder must sleep with his head either to the east or to the south; any other position is unhealthy. In proper time, under the influence of an auspicious planet and in an auspicious moment he should go to his wife if she is not unbathed, sick, unwell, unwilling, angry, pregnant, hungry or over-fed. He should also be free from all these imperfections and should be neatly dressed and adorned and excited by tenderness and affection. Having bathed, wearing garlands, using perfumes, delighted and animated by desire he should go to his wife—not being hungry and excited with anxiety. There are certain days on which the use of unguents, flesh and women is prohibited as the eighth and fourteenth lunar days, new-moon and full-moon and the entrance of the sun into a new sign. On these occasions the wise should control their appetites and engage in the worship of the celestials as laid down in scripture, in meditation and prayer. And he, who acts otherwise, will be doomed to a hell where he will be constrained to live upon ordure. A man should not excite his desires by medicines nor satisfy them with unnatural objects or in public or holy places. A man should not go to a woman under a huge tree, in the courtyard, in a place of pilgrimage, in pasturage, where four streets meet, in a cremation ground, in a garden or in the waters. On all these occasions mentioned before in the morning or in the evening or being unclean the wise should not cohabit with women. If a man goes to a woman during the Parva he loses wealth, if during the day he is visited with sin, if he cohabits with a woman on ground he loses his fame. A man should not think voluptuously of another's wife, nor should, he speak to her for that purpose; for such a wight will be born in his next life as a creeping insect. The cohabitation with another's wife is a source of fear to him both in this life and in the next—for in this he loses his longevity and in the next he is doomed to hell. Considering all these things a man should approach his own wife in proper season or even at other times".
